purpose: Test two explicitly exploratory relations of the already published native1Hz spectral maxima, preserving every one of the original five peaks. Not a general period detector, clock fit or RPM estimate
input: Exact F2_idle_observation_v1/audit1 display_only_low_band_peaks, source6..12s in three2s blocks; no rereading, filtering or fitting vehicle PCM
anchor_hypothesis: First three previously ranked strong peaks are proposed orders2,3,5. This hypothesis was chosen after seeing the F2 spectrum; it is not independent validation of the peak selector
bin_interpretation: Literal native-bin boxes under an isolated stationary-tone rounding assumption ONLY, not calibrated confidence, a guarantee under drift/interference/noise or a fundamental-frequency prior
method: Intersect anchor frequency boxes divided by proposed orders; enumerate every integer order for each remaining peak compatible with that interval, then intersect all boxes. Never drop the82Hz observation or fill empty intersections
controls: Exact algebra: integer harmonics admit smaller subharmonics, missing fundamental stays ambiguous, fifth-only line rejects simple bank pattern, independent line/inconsistent anchors/unrelated frequency lists reject both, rounded-bin boundary remains possible
audit: Independent exact Fraction interval/branch arithmetic and source identity; do not turn compatibility into proof of a physical period
